subject: Pilot capacity split and legal checklist before extension
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@mediwell.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: Gabe Torres <gabe@mediwell.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot wrap + ask about short extension and capacity split

Hi Stephanie,

Quick one — the team ran into a blocker in our integration tests and we'd like to request a short 2-week extension on the time-boxed pilot while we get a production data connector validated. Before we sign off internally, procurement asked two questions I couldn't answer:

1) Would Redwood allow us to convert unused run-time (we're likely to be underutilized week 4) into a capacity credit for later use, or do you only offer time extensions?
2) We have a preference to split our pilot commitment into a small seat/license bucket (for engineers debugging) plus a capacity bucket for model tokens. Can you confirm whether that's supported and whether packaging it that way affects pricing/discounts?

If we can get a simple amendment and a short SOW update we can route through procurement this week. Attached our internal integration log (small) showing where we stalled.

Thanks,
Olivia
Olivia Park
Director, ML Partnerships
MediWell Health

Attachment: integration_log_apr01.txt (text)
From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@mediwell.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot wrap + ask about short extension and capacity split

Hi Olivia — thanks for the note and the log, that helps. Short answers up front: yes, we can do a short 2-week extension and we support splitting the pilot into a seat bucket + capacity token bucket. How that maps to pricing depends on whether you want reserved seats (fixed monthly) or transient seat access billed against usage.

Proposed options (high level):
- Option A: 2-week time extension, no change to structure. 10% one-time extension credit on unused run-time if you commit to the extension within 48h.
- Option B: Convert anticipated unused run-time into a capacity credit now (applied to a future 90-day runway) + add 2 speciality seats for engineers. We can offer a 15% credit on converted tokens if you commit to a 3-month follow-on pilot.
- Option C: Swap to seat-heavy packaging (X engineer seats + Y capacity), which requires a small SOW amendment and procurement ok (pricing tiers change; I can show the delta).

I'll loop in Legal/Finance (David) and our CS lead (Marissa) to confirm the SOW language and the conversion mechanics. I'm attaching a draft SOW with placeholders for the capacity/seat split and our usage report so you can see where the run-rate sits.

Next steps: if you can say whether you prefer Option B (convert + 2-seat add) or Option C (repackage), I'll get a redline back today and aim to have DocuSign ready tomorrow.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: POC_SOW_v2.pdf, usage_report_apr.csv
From: david_kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot wrap + ask about short extension and capacity split

Looping in procurement/legal notes — short summary for SOW redline:
- We can accept conversion of unused run-time to a one-time capacity credit applied to a future 90-day period. Need to cap the convertible amount to avoid revenue recognition issues.
- For a 2-week extension we can offer a 10% invoice credit or a 15% credit if they take Option B and commit to a 3-month paid follow-on.
- Include a brief Data Processing Addendum (DPA) clause and a reference to the SOC2 evidence bundle. Procurement will want explicit retention and audit log language.

I'll prepare a redline and a short amendment clause ("Pilot Amendment A") that specifies the seat vs capacity buckets, conversion formula, and the DocuSign paths.

-David
David Kim
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai, Olivia Park <olivia.park@mediwell.ai>
Cc: Gabe Torres <gabe@mediwell.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot wrap + ask about short extension and capacity split

Thanks everyone — Olivia, from our CS side we recommend Option B. A practical way we've run this before:
- We convert reported unused run-time up to 30% of the remaining pilot allocation into a token credit at a 15% uplift (i.e., customer gets +15% tokens on the converted units as a good-will).
- Add two temporary engineer seats for the 2-week extension at a flat rate (covers support & priority routing).
- If you sign the 3-month follow-on within 30 days, we'll apply a 10% recurring discount to the follow-on committed capacity.

Olivia — I'll attach a short checklist for procurement (SOC2 link, DPA summary, sample SOW amendment language). If that looks good we can issue a redlined SOW and DocuSign.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: procurement_checklist_for_mediwell.pdf
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@mediwell.ai>

Subject: Re: Pilot wrap + ask about short extension and capacity split

Stephanie/Marissa/David — thanks for moving quickly on this and for the flexible options. Procurement reviewed the checklist and has two final asks before we can sign: 1) limit on convertible amount (30% cap is fine), and 2) inclusion of a short audit log retention clause (we need 12 months, spelled out).

We accept Option B with the 2-week extension and conversion of up to 30% of unused run-time into token credit (with the +15% uplift). Please send the redlined SOW and DocuSign link. We prefer the engineer seats billed as a fixed fee for the extension.

I'll route internally to get a sign-off and expect to return the signed DocuSign within 48 hours once we receive it. Appreciate the clear checklist — that made procurement's job easier.

Best,
Olivia
